MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  BUDGET STUDY SESSION
  MAY 30, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR HUFF at 12:12 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

5.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  RESIDENTIAL SOLID WASTE, RECYCLABLE MATERIALS AND ORGANIC
  WASTE COLLECTION SERVICE ROUTE SCHEDULE CHANGE PROPOSAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the residential waste, recycling,
  and organic waste collection service route schedule from one day per week to
  three days per week based upon the proposed route map and list as provided by
  Waste Management, effective July 31, 2023.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Waste Management Subcommittee members COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN and
MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ outlined the history of the Subcommittee’s discussions with
Waste Management, in order to reach this recommended route change, reducing the
amount of time trucks spend in the community, and ensuring the trucks are off of Palos
Verdes Drive North during peak traffic times.

Erick Quintero, Waste Management Public Sector Services Manager further explained
how Waste Management will reduce the number of trucks with the proposed schedule
and routes.

Assistant City Manager Davis outlined the communication plan to get the new schedule
out to the community, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via
eComment. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
ADJOURNED MEETING - BUDGET STUDY SESSION  1
MAY 30, 2023
   APPROVE THE RESIDENTIAL WASTE, RECYCLING, AND ORGANIC
  WASTE COLLECTION SERVICE ROUTE SCHEDULE FROM ONE DAY
  PER WEEK TO THREE DAYS PER WEEK BASED UPON THE
  PROPOSED ROUTE MAP AND LIST AS PROVIDED BY WASTE
  MANAGEMENT, EFFECTIVE JULY 31, 2023

6.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 AND 2024-25 BUDGET STUDY SESSION

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the information and discuss the
  programs and services to allow staff to prepare the final budget for presentation
  and public hearing on June 27, 2023.

City Manager Grammer introduced the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 and 2024-25 proposed
budget and provided an overview, highlighting the steady increases in building permit
revenue, property tax revenue and sales tax revenue. He noted that the budget continues
funding essential programming including public safety, tree trimming and street sweeping.
Using special funds, general funds, and federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds,
capital improvement projects are planned for such as storm drain infrastructure, street
resurfacing, intersection enhancements and a variety of park improvements. The General
Fund operating surplus is projected to be $1.9 million (18%), due primarily to greater than
expected building permit revenue. Park Facility Fees fund balance is projected to have
$1.2 million in additional revenues for FY 2023-24 and $1.3 million for FY 2024-25. Public
Safety remains to be the largest single-expenditure, with the Sheriff’s contract increase
of 7.63% which is reflected in the budget, as well as the City’s recently adopted Pension
Funding Policy. After meeting last week, the Audit/Finance Committee, comprised of
MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ AND COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, and staff
recommend allocating $300,000 for a lump sum payment to CalPERS to go toward the
City’s Unfunded Accrued Liability (UAL).

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued about the City’s current UAL balance.

Discussion ensued about the City’s increasing property values and property tax revenue.

Community Development Director Naughton explained the anticipated building permit
revenue in FY 2024-25 is due to the proposed 90-unit residential project at the Peninsula
Center, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Discussion ensued about the City’s annual tree trimming maintenance schedule.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead outlined necessary maintenance and
upgrades planned for City Hall, including a roof replacement, painting, and some interior
work in the next two fiscal years, which will be presented to the City Council at the next
Policy Development Session, in response to MAYOR HUFF.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead and Assistant City Manager Davis explained
the capital improvement projects planned for Ernie Howlett Park during the next two fiscal
years using Park Facility Fees, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

MAYOR HUFF requested that the Palos Verdes Drive North/Dapplegray School
Intersection Improvement Project be more clearly identified in the budget.

Discussion ensued about the higher than anticipated cost of the Founders Park Project
and possible ways to reduce the overall cost. City Manager Grammer indicated that staff
will return to the City Council on June 27 with the bid results, along with options to reduce
the cost of the project.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
ADJOURNED MEETING - BUDGET STUDY SESSION  2
MAY 30, 2023
 MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ inquired about the $15,000 budgeted for brush clearance.
Maintenance Supervisor Goldsmith discussed upcoming plans for brush clearance and
weed removal in response to the heavy rains and “super bloom.”

City Manager Grammer explained that the Emergency Management personnel budget
increased in the upcoming fiscal year to better capture the time Management Analyst
Slawson spends on that activity, and that an equal amount was reduced elsewhere in the
budget, in response to MAYOR HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via
eComment. No public testimony was received.

It was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to incorporate the changes
discussed and prepare the final budget for presentation and public hearing on June 27,
2023.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

At 1:27 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the meeting, to the Regular City Council meeting
at 7:00 p.m. June 13, 2023.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor
